doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Forging a letter to meet Duke Ellington in Detroit
summary: At 18 she sent Duke a letter signed with Spike Hughes's name, was received backstage and became family.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Absolutely. I wanted to ask you about Chicago. So this is early ‘30s? Mid-30s?

Mid. I left Chicago in ‘36. And probably I started with Duke in Detroit at the Fox Theater. And I was 18 and from Toronto. And of course Duke was Duke. And I was darned if I wasn’t going to go backstage. I didn’t know what backstage was all about, but I was going to go. So I did. And you know Duke had a marvelous sense of humor, and a marvelous feeling for life, so I knew it would be fun, interesting. And so when this gal appeared, you know, and sent up her — I sent him a letter on English note paper. Stanley and I had both, separately, without knowing one another, we’d both heard those wonderful concerts in London. And so I sent a letter, supposedly signed by Spike Hughes, who was a favorite of his, saying that this girl has probably got something to offer you. Receive her. And this just played into Duke’s hands. He had me ushered up. Mill was his girl from a long time. So I went in the dressing room, and Duke received me in a most marvelous fashion, and of course I was honored. And I had the brass to tell him what I thought was the best in his work, and how I didn’t really appreciate Barney Bigard. And of course he loves Barney. Because I liked the other type, I liked the New Orleans more than Barney. Barney was typical of New Orleans, but anyway, so he listened to me with the greatest kindness. And I said, “Would you honor us by coming and having afternoon tea one day this week?” And he said yes. And they had afternoon tea, and I saw my letter up on the mirror, and I knew it shouldn’t be there. Why was my © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

letter on the mirror? With all the fans he’d had, why was mine up there? And I looked at him and we looked at each other and I said, “I probably shouldn’t have forged it, should I?” And he said, “Oh I’m so pleased you did.” So we were friends forever after you know. That was wonderful. So he took me downstairs and said to the guys, “This is family, guys, lay off.” And it was wonderful, because I was family, and for the rest of my life, and for as long as he lived, I was family, and that was the greatest thing that ever happened to me.
